content.text: Found it. B1-PC2 has subnet mask `/16` instead of `/24`. This causes it to think 10.1.2.x and 10.1.3.x are on-link (same subnet) and try ARP directly instead of routing through the gateway. The 10.2.x.x addresses work because they fall outside even the /16. Fix the subnet mask.

content.text:
All clean. Everything is saved and persistent. Here's the report.

---

## Report

### Faults Found

| # | Device | Fault | Actual | Design | Fix |
|---|--------|-------|--------|--------|-----|
| 1 | Hub-A | OSPF MD5 key on eth0 wrong case | `LabArea0key` (lowercase k) | `LabArea0Key` (uppercase K) | `delete protocols ospf interface eth0 authentication md5 key-id 1 md5-key LabArea0key` then `set ... LabArea0Key`, commit, save. This restored the HQ-Edge to Hub-A area 0 adjacency. |
| 2 | Branch-2 | ether1 MTU set to 1400 | MTU 1400 | Platform default (1500) | `/interface ethernet set [find default-name=ether1] mtu=1500`. The MTU mismatch caused the OSPF adjacency with Hub-A to stick in ExStart/Exchange. |
| 3 | Branch-2 | LAN OSPF interface-template missing passive | Not passive | Passive | `/routing ospf interface-template set [find networks=10.1.2.0/24] passive` |
| 4 | Hub-B | Virtual link peer configured as IP address | Peer `172.16.10.9` (Hub-A's eth3 IP) | Peer `10.255.0.2` (Hub-A's router ID) | `delete protocols ospf area 10 virtual-link 172.16.10.9`, `set protocols ospf area 10 virtual-link 10.255.0.2 authentication md5 key-id 1 md5-key LabArea0Key`, commit, save. Virtual links use router IDs, not interface IPs. |
| 5 | Branch-4 | Area 20 not configured as stub | `type=default` | `type=stub` | `/routing ospf area set [find name=area20] type=stub`. All routers in a stub area must agree on the stub flag; Branch-4 had a plain area, preventing adjacency with Hub-B. |
| 6 | Branch-3 | Spurious firewall rule dropping OSPF | `action=drop chain=forward protocol=ospf` present | No firewall on Branch-3 per design | `/ip firewall filter remove [find action=drop chain=forward]` |
| 7 | Branch-4 | Guest firewall rule accepts all (no connection-state) | First rule: `action=accept chain=forward` (no filter) | Stateful: accept only established,related | `/ip firewall filter set [find comment~"allow return"] connection-state=established,related`. Without this, the accept-all rule made the guest drop rules unreachable. |
| 8 | Hub-A | Area 10 summary range wrong mask | `10.1.0.0/24` | `10.1.0.0/16` | `delete protocols ospf area 10 range 10.1.0.0/24`, `set protocols ospf area 10 range 10.1.0.0/16`, commit, save. |
| 9 | HQ-Edge | BGP local-preference on wrong route-map | ISP-B-IN sets LP 200 (ISP-B preferred) | ISP-A-IN should set LP 200 (ISP-A preferred) | `delete policy route-map ISP-B-IN rule 10 set local-preference`, `set policy route-map ISP-A-IN rule 10 set local-preference 200`, commit, save. |
| 10 | HQ-Edge | NAT rule 110 wrong outbound interface | `outbound-interface name eth1` | `outbound-interface name eth2` (ISP-B link) | `set nat source rule 110 outbound-interface name eth2`, commit, save. Both NAT rules pointed at eth1 (ISP-A); traffic leaving via ISP-B wasn't NATed. |
| 11 | HQ-Edge | OSPF default-information originate always | `always` present | No `always` (conditional origination) | `delete protocols ospf default-information originate always`, `set protocols ospf default-information originate`, commit, save. Design requires HQ-Edge to only originate the default when it has one itself. |
| 12 | B1-PC2 | Subnet mask /16 instead of /24 | `10.1.1.11/16` | `10.1.1.11/24` | `ip addr del 10.1.1.11/16 dev eth0`, `ip addr add 10.1.1.11/24 dev eth0`, `ip route add default via 10.1.1.1 dev eth0 metric 1 onlink`, and updated `/etc/network/interfaces`. The /16 mask caused B1-PC2 to ARP directly for 10.1.2.x and 10.1.3.x hosts instead of routing through the gateway. |

### Verification

**1. Adjacencies and sessions**

| Adjacency | State |
|-----------|-------|
| eBGP HQ-Edge to ISP-A (203.0.113.1, AS 65100) | Established |
| eBGP HQ-Edge to ISP-B (203.0.113.5, AS 65200) | Established |
| OSPF HQ-Edge to Hub-A (area 0) | Full |
| OSPF Hub-A to Branch-1 (area 10) | Full |
| OSPF Hub-A to Branch-2 (area 10) | Full |
| OSPF Hub-A to Branch-3 (area 10) | Full |
| OSPF Branch-3 to Hub-B (area 10) | Full |
| OSPF Hub-B to Branch-4 (area 20) | Full |
| OSPF Hub-A to Hub-B virtual link | Full |

**2. Routing tables**

- HQ-Edge: default via ISP-A (203.0.113.1, LP 200) is best; ISP-B backup present (203.0.113.5, LP 100). 8.8.8.8/32 via ISP-A, 1.1.1.1/32 via ISP-B. No routes advertised to either ISP. OSPF routes to 10.1.0.0/16 and 10.2.0.0/16 (summaries only).
- Hub-A, Hub-B, Branch-1/2/3: default route via OSPF from HQ-Edge. All have routes covering every lab subnet.
- Branch-4: default route from Hub-B (area 20 stub default). Sees 10.1.0.0/16 as inter-area summary. No external routes (totally stubby).
- HQ-Edge sees area 10 LANs only as 10.1.0.0/16 and area 20 LANs only as 10.2.0.0/16.

**3. Host reachability**

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Non-guest to non-guest (56 pairs) | 56/56 pass |
| Guest to guest (2 pairs) | 2/2 pass |
| Guest to non-guest isolation (32 pairs) | 32/32 correctly blocked |
| All PCs to 8.8.8.8 | 10/10 pass |
| All PCs to 1.1.1.1 | 10/10 pass |

**4. Backup path**

ISP-B's default route is present as BGP backup (LP 100). All PCs can ping 1.1.1.1 (via ISP-B), confirming the ISP-B link and its NAT work.

**5. Config persistence**

All VyOS changes committed and saved. All MikroTik changes are immediate and persistent. B1-PC2's `/etc/network/interfaces` updated.

### Unresolved

**Area 20 summary leak into area 10:** Hub-B's `area 20 range 10.2.0.0/16` correctly generates the /16 summary and correctly suppresses the individual /24 routes into area 0 (HQ-Edge sees only 10.2.0.0/16). However, FRR 10.5.1 does not suppress the individual 10.2.1.0/24 and 10.2.2.0/24 summary LSAs into area 10 (the virtual link's transit area). Area 10 routers see both 10.2.0.0/16 and the individual /24s. The configuration matches the design; this appears to be a FRR platform limitation with area range suppression into the transit area of a virtual link. The extra routes cause no functional impact (traffic follows the same path, and the /16 summary is present). Clearing the OSPF process and toggling the range config were both attempted without effect.
